projects.title: Parametric Exoskeleton Building
projects.description: A twisting, tapering tower organized around a public passage, with an exterior exoskeleton and selected floors that bridge across the opening.

blocks.text: For ARCH655 Project 1, I explored how a vertical passage could become the organizing idea for a tower. The building tapers and twists around a route that begins at the ground and continues through the floors. A curved exoskeleton follows the changing profile, tying the two sides together while keeping the opening visible.

The passage is defined by a guide curve that shifts across the tower as it rises. Its path controls where the opening moves and changes direction, turning a straight slot into a continuous route through the building. Most floor plates stop at the opening. Every third floor crosses it as a bridge, connecting the two sides while leaving the levels between open. The exoskeleton frames this movement and helps the tower read as one connected form.
Before and after: the curve that defines the cut

The first view shows the guide curve highlighted in yellow against the tower. In the second, the curve is hidden so the passage it guides is easier to read. Together, the views show how the curve sets the route of the cut and how the floor plates respond to that opening.

blocks.caption: Guide curve: the path defining the passage is highlighted in yellow.
blocks.content: The curve shifts across the tower as it rises, setting the passage route.

blocks.caption: Resulting cut: the guide curve is hidden to show the passage.
blocks.content: The opening follows the curve, with selected floor plates connecting across it.

blocks.caption: Front view showing the passage and selected floor bridges.
blocks.content: Most slabs stop at the cut, while every third slab spans the opening.

blocks.text: Four precedents helped me think about movement, structure, and carved space. [The Klein Bottle House](https://www.mcbridecharlesryan.com.au/project/klein-bottle-house/) uses a spiral to shape a sequence of spaces. [Arnhem Central Transfer Terminal](https://www.archdaily.com/777495/arnhem-central-transfer-terminal-unstudio) links movement and form through a twisting structure. [One Thousand Museum](https://www.odparchitects.com/project/one-thousand-museum/) makes its curving exoskeleton central to the tower identity. [Morpheus Hotel](https://www.archdaily.com/896433/morpheus-hotel-zaha-hadid-architects) connects public spaces through carved voids and bridges. I used these projects as reference points, then developed a distinct tower organized around its own passage.

The Grasshopper definition turns that design sequence into linked operations. The tower profile, taper, and twist establish the outer form. The guide curve then defines the passage route, and the floor logic responds to the cut: most slabs terminate at the opening, while every third slab bridges across. The exoskeleton follows the changing tower profile. Grouped controls and notes make the inputs easier to follow and let the form update as its dimensions change.

blocks.caption: Grasshopper definition: grouped controls and geometry logic for the tower, passage, floors, and exoskeleton.
blocks.content: The definition shows how the design inputs feed the tower geometry and how the passage, floor plates, and exterior frame are generated from those relationships.

blocks.caption: Elevated view of the completed tower and its central passage.
blocks.content: This view shows the passage depth and how the exterior frame relates to the floor plates.

blocks.text: After establishing the form, I added a separate analysis group in Grasshopper to describe the tower surface. It calculates surface area and centroid, samples the surface at 121 UV points, and reports principal curvature, curvature directions, Gaussian curvature, and mean curvature. A bounding box measures the overall X, Y, and Z dimensions. The analysis outputs are saved in project1_analyses.gh, with a companion Rhino file, project1_analyses.3dm, containing the labeled curvature and dimension visualization.

The AI images explored a possible atmosphere for the passage, terraces, and exterior frame before the model was complete. They helped test the contrast between a glazed tower and an open route through its center. These images communicate a visual concept; the Rhino and Grasshopper screenshots document how the design was modeled.

blocks.caption: AI concept 1: a planted passage spirals through the tower.
blocks.content: This view imagines the opening as a sequence of outdoor terraces and shared spaces.

blocks.caption: AI concept 2: an alternate view of the tower and its open frame.
blocks.content: This study explores how the passage and exterior structure might meet the surrounding landscape.
